title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing and padding minimization heuristics v22
author: Asha Gupta
description: Motivation: production traffic shows tail latency and wasted GPU cycles due to naive bucketing that groups sequences with large padding overhead. This PR refines the dynamic batching heuristics by introducing adaptive bucketing based on empirical seqlen distributions, an online padding-cost estimator, and improved scheduling hooks to reduce worst-case padding while preserving throughput and token-level latency targets. High level changes: 1) Introduce SeqlenHistogram class that maintains a lightweight sliding-window histogram per worker to estimate seqlen distribution with bounded memory. 2) AdaptiveBucketer that chooses bucket boundaries to minimize expected padded tokens given current histogram and a configurable max-latency SLO. 3) PaddingCostEstimator that models extra token cost and integrates with the scheduler to prefer filling slots with low marginal padding cost. 4) Small kernel-level change to the continuous batching path to permit partial-copy KV-cache layout for mixed-length batches reducing memory traffic for short contexts. 5) Backwards-compatible config knobs: seqlen_bucket_count, histogram_window_ms, max_padding_ratio, and enable_partial_kv_copy. Benchmarks: reproducible lab tests (BERT-like and LLaMA-variant) on p4d.24 with mixed seqlen workloads show 18-24% reduction in padded tokens and 7-12% end-to-end token throughput increase for 95th-percentile latency constrained scenarios. In low-latency SLOs we see a 10-40ms median latency decrease for common chat workloads. Rollout and safety: feature gated behind enable_adaptive_bucketing; default off and will be enabled via canary with traffic shaping. Includes smoke tests, unit tests for histogram and bucketer, and integration test exercising mixed-length continuous batching. See linked Linear items for rollout plan. This description summarizes code changes, rationale, tests, benchmarks, and rollout guidance.
commits: Implement AdaptiveBucketer and integrate with Scheduler
Enable partial KV cache copy in continuous-batch path
Fix race in histogram update under high concurrency
Bench: add workloads and analysis scripts
review_comments: Michael Chen: Nice work overall. Can you clarify how the histogram window_ms interacts with autoscaling rollbacks? We should avoid oscillations.
Asha Gupta: Good point. Updated the PR to include hysteresis and a separate autoscale_lock window to prevent frequent bucketing flips (see seqlen_histogram.cpp).
Ravi Patel: The partial KV copy change looks risky for older quantized kernels. Can we gate it behind a safe runtime check?
Asha Gupta: Gate added: enable_partial_kv_copy and runtime check for quantization-compatible formats. Added integration test for quantized path.
Elena Morales: Add a short note in docs about how to interpret max_padding_ratio and tradeoffs for latency vs throughput.
Asha Gupta: Docs updated in docs/runtime/batching.md with examples.
CI: flake8 found minor style issues in tests; fixed in follow-up commit.
release_notes: Performance: Adaptive sequence-length bucketing reduces padded tokens and improves throughput for mixed-length workloads. Introduces config knobs: seqlen_bucket_count, histogram_window_ms, max_padding_ratio, enable_partial_kv_copy. Default disabled; enable via feature flag for canary rollout.
